definition: The corpus striatum is a brain region in each cerebral hemisphere, positioned in front of and to the side of the thalamus. It is made of striped gray and white matter, including the neostriatum and paleostriatum, with gray matter from the caudate nucleus and lentiform nucleus and white matter from the internal capsule.

The definition does not reflect the packet’s explicit parenthetical identification of paleostriatum as globus pallidus.

The definition says the gray matter includes “caudate nucleus and lentiform nucleus” and white matter includes “internal capsule”; the packet supports caudate nucleus and lentiform nucleus, but it also defines the lentiform nucleus as globus pallidus and putamen. That added structural specificity is present in the packet; the provided definition omits “putamen” and the internal capsule mapping is supported.

The paleostriatum/globus pallidus relationship is a substantive structural claim that is not explicitly supported in the definition as written (it is asserted only as “paleostriatum”), whereas the packet provides the explicit synonym/identification.
